name: Mercury
lede: A small, cratered messenger of the Sun — extremes of heat and cold on a slow-spinning iron-rich core.

landmark.label: Caloris Basin
landmark.blurb: One of the largest impact basins in the solar system — roughly 1,550 km across, mapped by Mariner 10 and MESSENGER.

missions.name: Mariner 10
missions.note: First close flybys; mapped about half the surface.

missions.name: MESSENGER
missions.note: First orbiter; global geology, magnetic field, and volatile ices in polar shadows.

missions.name: BepiColombo
missions.note: ESA/JAXA dual-spacecraft orbiter en route for detailed mapping.

researchNotes: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. Its day is longer than its year: one solar day lasts about 176 Earth days because of a 3:2 spin–orbit resonance.
Despite scorching dayside temperatures, radar and MESSENGER data show water ice and organic-rich materials in permanently shadowed polar craters.
The planet has a large iron core and a weak global magnetic field — unusual for such a slow rotator — pointing to an active dynamo in the deep interior.
folklore: Named for the Roman messenger god. Classical astrology linked Mercury to quick wit and travel; that lore is cultural history, not geology.
carlFocus: Emphasize Caloris Basin, the 3:2 resonance, polar ice in shadow, and Mariner 10 / MESSENGER heritage. Keep replies short for speech.
